portName: Port of Naples (Stazione Marittima, Molo Angioino)
seoTitle: Naples cruise port guide: walk to town, train to Pompeii
seoDescription: Naples cruise port 2026: dock at Stazione Marittima, 10–15 min walk to Plebiscito. Circumvesuviana to Pompeii €3.30, about 35 min; Pompeii ticket €20.
quickAnswer: Ships dock at the Stazione Marittima on Molo Angioino, right in the city; Piazza del Plebiscito is 10–15 minutes on foot and Spaccanapoli about 15–20. For Pompeii, take metro Line 1 to Garibaldi and the Circumvesuviana Sorrento line to Pompei Scavi: €3.30 and about 35 minutes (2026). Be back on board 90 minutes before all-aboard if your return depends on the train.
intro: Naples is one of the few big Mediterranean ports where you step off the ship into the city centre. Castel Nuovo is across the road and the old town is a 15-minute walk. The decision is how to split the day between Naples itself and the sites around the bay: Pompeii and Herculaneum by the Circumvesuviana commuter train, or Capri and Sorrento by ferry from Molo Beverello next door. The train is cheap but crowded and old, so leave a wide margin.

terminals.name: Stazione Marittima (Molo Angioino)
terminals.notes: Main cruise terminal, run by Terminal Napoli, with shops and a pharmacy inside. Castel Nuovo and Piazza Municipio are directly opposite; Municipio metro (Line 1) is a few minutes' walk.

terminals.name: Molo Beverello
terminals.notes: Next door. Hydrofoils and fast ferries to Capri, Sorrento and Ischia leave from here. Not the cruise terminal, though cruisers often confuse the two.

walkability.detail: Flat walk from the terminal past Castel Nuovo to Piazza del Plebiscito and Galleria Umberto I (10–15 minutes), or up Via Toledo and into Spaccanapoli (about 15–20 minutes). Pavements are uneven and traffic is heavy; cross at lights. The Archaeological Museum is about 10 minutes beyond Spaccanapoli, uphill.

transportSections.detail: The simplest way into Naples. Turn right out of the terminal for Piazza del Plebiscito, or cross Piazza Municipio and head up Via Toledo for Spaccanapoli.

transportSections.cost: Single and 90-minute tickets about €1.30–1.80; check at the machine
transportSections.detail: Municipio station is a few minutes from the terminal. Line 1 runs to Duomo and Garibaldi (for the Circumvesuviana and the main railway station) and to Toledo and Museo. Several stations are known for their art design.

transportSections.time: About 35 min Garibaldi to Pompei Scavi
transportSections.detail: Take the Sorrento line from Napoli Garibaldi (underground platforms, usually platform 3, stairs only) or from Porta Nolana, its first stop. Get off at Pompei Scavi–Villa dei Misteri, about 50 m from the Porta Marina entrance; not Pompei Santuario. Trains run about every 30 minutes. Tap a contactless card or phone in and out at the gates, or validate a paper ticket at the yellow machines; fines for unvalidated tickets are around €50. Trains are often crowded and only newer ones have air conditioning.
Tourist service on the same line with reserved seats and air conditioning. Runs mid-March to mid-October, with only four departures in each direction, so fit the day around its timetable.

transportSections.cost: Fixed tourist fares exist for main destinations; ask for the fixed fare before you start
transportSections.detail: White licensed taxis wait at the terminal. Naples traffic is slow; for Pompeii the train is usually as quick.

returnTiming.rule: From Pompeii, catch a train back no later than 3 hours before all-aboard (14:30 for a 17:30 all-aboard). From the old town, start walking back 75 minutes before.
returnTiming.detail: The train is about 35 minutes, plus the metro from Garibaldi and the walk to the terminal (about 25 minutes together), and trains run only every 30 minutes. Strikes and breakdowns on the Circumvesuviana are not rare. From Spaccanapoli the walk is 15–20 minutes, but allow for heat and crowds.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: If a train is cancelled, take the next one; if the line is down, take a licensed taxi from Pompei Scavi and agree the fare first. In Naples, the terminal is walkable from anywhere central. Call the port agent number in your daily programme if you will be late.

diyVsExcursion.ship: Coach included in ship tours; price varies by line
diyVsExcursion.diy: €6.60 return on the Circumvesuviana, plus metro (2026)
€20 basic, €25 Pompeii+ with the suburban villas (2026)

diyVsExcursion.ship: Varies by line; check your cruise planner
diyVsExcursion.diy: About €27: return train and basic Pompeii ticket (2026)

diyVsExcursion.ship: Walking tours sold by most lines

excursionAdvice: Naples itself needs no excursion. For Pompeii, the train works for confident travellers on a weekday with no strike, but the ship's coach is worth it in July and August heat, on a rail strike day, for anyone who struggles with stairs and crowded trains, or if you want Pompeii and Vesuvius together, which is hard to do by public transport in one call. The Amalfi Coast is too far for a safe independent day.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes docking at 08:00 and a Pompeii ticket booked for the 09:00–13:00 entry window.

steps.what: Leave the ship, walk 5 minutes to Municipio metro and take Line 1 to Garibaldi.
Circumvesuviana Sorrento line from Napoli Garibaldi to Pompei Scavi–Villa dei Misteri (about 35 minutes).
Enter Pompeii at Porta Marina. Forum, baths, the House of the Faun, the amphitheatre route; about three hours.
Leave the site and catch a train back to Naples, aiming for one before 13:30.
From Garibaldi, walk or take Line 1 one stop to Duomo. Lunch at a pizzeria on Via dei Tribunali.
Walk Spaccanapoli and San Gregorio Armeno, then Piazza del Gesù.
Down Via Toledo to Galleria Umberto I and Piazza del Plebiscito.
Back on board, 90 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: Pompeii
sights.why: The Roman city buried by Vesuvius in AD 79, about 35 minutes by train.
sights.cost: €20 basic; €25 Pompeii+ (2026); free under 18 and on the first Sunday of the month
sights.tip: Tickets are named and limited to 20,000 a day in timed windows from mid-March to mid-October; buy only from the official seller (Vivaticket via pompeiisites.org). Bring water and a hat; there is little shade.

sights.name: Spaccanapoli and Via dei Tribunali
sights.why: The straight streets that cut through the Greek-Roman grid of the old town, lined with churches and pizzerias.
sights.tip: Detour into San Gregorio Armeno for the nativity-figure workshops.

sights.name: Cappella Sansevero
sights.why: Home of the Veiled Christ marble sculpture.
sights.tip: Booking is required and tickets are named; closed on Tuesdays except some summer dates. Book online up to 60 days ahead.

sights.name: National Archaeological Museum (MANN)
sights.why: The best finds from Pompeii and Herculaneum, including mosaics and frescoes.
sights.tip: Closed on Tuesdays. A good alternative to Pompeii on a hot or wet day; Museo station on Line 1.

sights.name: Piazza del Plebiscito and the Royal Palace
sights.why: The city's main square, 10–15 minutes from the ship.
sights.cost: Free to the square; palace charged (check the official site)
sights.tip: Coffee at Gran Caffè Gambrinus on the corner.

sights.name: Castel Nuovo (Maschio Angioino)
sights.why: The medieval castle directly opposite the cruise terminal.
sights.cost: Free to view; interior charged (check on the day)
sights.tip: Useful if you have an hour spare before reboarding.

sights.name: Galleria Umberto I
sights.why: A 19th-century glass-roofed shopping arcade off Via Toledo.
sights.tip: Good shelter from rain or sun on the walk back.

beaches.name: Via Caracciolo and Rotonda Diaz seafront
beaches.howToGetThere: Walk west from Piazza del Plebiscito along the seafront past Castel dell'Ovo.
beaches.note: Rocks and concrete platforms rather than sand. Locals swim here in summer, but Naples is not a beach port.

food.where: L'Antica Pizzeria da Michele, Via Cesare Sersale, near Garibaldi
Gino e Toto Sorbillo, Via dei Tribunali
Sfogliatelle Attanasio, Vico Ferrovia, near Garibaldi station
Gran Caffè Gambrinus, Piazza Trieste e Trento
Pizzeria Di Matteo, Via dei Tribunali

commonMistakes.fix: Stay on to Pompei Scavi–Villa dei Misteri; the entrance is right by the station.

commonMistakes.mistake: Buying Pompeii tickets from a non-official site or tout.
commonMistakes.fix: Since March 2026 only Vivaticket via the official site issues valid tickets. They are named, so book in the name of each visitor.

commonMistakes.mistake: Turning up at Pompeii without a ticket in summer.
commonMistakes.fix: Daily entries are capped at 20,000, mostly in the morning window; book a few days ahead.

commonMistakes.mistake: Not validating a paper Circumvesuviana ticket.
commonMistakes.fix: Stamp it in the yellow machine or use tap-in, tap-out with a contactless card.

commonMistakes.mistake: Visiting Cappella Sansevero or MANN on a Tuesday.
commonMistakes.fix: Both close on Tuesdays (Sansevero opens some summer Tuesdays). Check before you plan.

commonMistakes.mistake: Cutting the return from Pompeii fine.
commonMistakes.fix: Trains run every 30 minutes and can be cancelled. Be on a train three hours before all-aboard.

safety: Naples has a reputation that exceeds the reality for daytime visitors, but petty theft is common. Pickpockets work around Garibaldi station, on the Circumvesuviana and in crowded old-town streets. Bag and phone snatches from scooters happen; keep phones away from the kerb side. The port area, Via Toledo and the old town are busy and generally safe in daylight. Traffic is the most immediate danger: cross at lights and watch for scooters on pavements.
scams: Unofficial guides and ticket sellers outside Pompeii and near the stations offering tours or 'skip-the-line' entry. Buy tickets only through the official site; touts' tickets may not scan, as tickets are named.
Taxis that do not start the meter or quote inflated fares to Pompeii or the port. Use white licensed taxis and ask for the fixed tourist fare before you start.
Pickpocketing on the Circumvesuviana, especially at Garibaldi and on crowded carriages. Keep bags zipped and in front.
Street sellers near Garibaldi offering 'new' phones or electronics that turn out to be fakes or empty boxes. Do not buy on the street.
accessibility: The Stazione Marittima is the easiest step-free point in the port. The walk to Piazza del Plebiscito is flat but pavements are uneven and kerbs high. Garibaldi's Circumvesuviana platforms are reported to have stairs only, and trains have steps, so Pompeii by train is difficult for wheelchair users. Pompeii's streets are rough basalt with high kerbs. A ship coach tour or an adapted taxi is the realistic choice for limited mobility.
rainyDay: The National Archaeological Museum is the best wet-day plan: it holds the finest objects from Pompeii and Herculaneum (closed Tuesdays). Cappella Sansevero, the Royal Palace and Galleria Umberto I are also indoors or covered. Pompeii in heavy rain is slippery and exposed. Underground tours of the old city also work in rain.
crowdTips: Pompeii is busiest from late morning, when coach groups arrive; the 09:00–13:00 window takes up to 15,000 of the 20,000 daily entries. Arriving at opening helps. Free first Sundays sell out fast. Circumvesuviana trains are fullest at weekday rush hours (roughly 07:30–09:00 and 17:30–19:00). In Naples, Spaccanapoli and Via dei Tribunali are packed at lunchtime and the best-known pizzerias have queues; eat early or late.

faqs.q: Is Naples cruise port walkable to the city?
faqs.a: Yes. The Stazione Marittima is in the city centre. Piazza del Plebiscito is 10–15 minutes on foot and Spaccanapoli about 15–20.
No. Ships dock at the Stazione Marittima on Molo Angioino.

faqs.q: How do I get from Naples cruise port to Pompeii?
faqs.a: Walk to Municipio, take metro Line 1 to Garibaldi, then the Circumvesuviana Sorrento line to Pompei Scavi–Villa dei Misteri. The train costs €3.30 and takes about 35 minutes (2026).

faqs.q: How much is a Pompeii ticket?
faqs.a: €20 for the basic ticket and €25 for Pompeii+, which adds the Villa of the Mysteries and other suburban villas (2026). Under-18s are free. Tickets are named and sold only through the official channel.

faqs.q: Is the Circumvesuviana reliable enough for a cruise day?
faqs.a: Usually, but it is crowded, trains run only every 30 minutes, and strikes happen. Check EAV notices the day before and be on a return train three hours before all-aboard.

faqs.q: What can I do in Naples in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Pompeii in the morning and the old town in the afternoon, or a full day in Naples: Spaccanapoli, Cappella Sansevero, the Archaeological Museum and Piazza del Plebiscito, all on foot or by Line 1.

faqs.q: Is Naples safe for cruise passengers?
faqs.a: Yes in daylight in the centre, with the usual care. Watch for pickpockets at Garibaldi and on trains, and keep phones away from passing scooters.

faqs.q: Are there beaches near Naples cruise port?
faqs.a: Not really. The nearest swimming is from rocks along Via Caracciolo, 20–30 minutes' walk. For sand, a ferry to Capri, Ischia or Procida is needed.
